title: Cluster G — Ivatsevichy-Kobryn-Dolyna I/II (P3484/P5938): DUPLICATE_REFUTED, but capacity is double-counted and length is unsourced

rows.recommendation: Do NOT merge, delete, or treat as a duplicate of P5938 -- three independent sources confirm this is a genuine two-string parallel system, not one pipe recorded twice. DO fix two real data-quality defects: (1) CapacityBcm/y=29.00 is the SYSTEM TOTAL for the whole two-line corridor, not this string's own capacity -- GEM's own prior researcher note on this row already says so ('The capacity number is total for the pipeline'), and the independent ISANS 2023 report puts the whole two-line system at ~30 bcm/y. Currently both rows show 29.00, so any roll-up that sums P3484+P5938 double-counts to 58 bcm/y against a real corridor total of ~29-30 bcm/y. Recommend either splitting to a documented per-string estimate (no source gives an explicit split; ~14.5-15 bcm/y each is the naive assumption, unverified) or, short of a source for the split, adding a ResearcherNotes flag on both rows warning against summing this figure. (2) LengthKnownKm=292.00 cites the ISANS 2023 PDF as its ref, but that PDF (independently re-fetched and full-text-extracted for this pass) contains NO length figure for this pipeline at all -- only diameter (1220mm, confirmed correct) and the ~30 bcm/y system total. The ref does not support the value it is attached to. Meanwhile Ukrtransgaz's own construction chronology (the operator's official corporate history) gives this string ('I нитка') a commissioning length of 357.7 km in 1976 -- matching this row's StartYear1 exactly, but not its length. Route to Update to re-source LengthKnownKm using the UTG chronology (noting the open question below about what territorial extent that figure represents).
rows.notes: StartYear1=1976 matches UTG chronology's dated entry for 'Івацевичі - Долина (І нитка)' verbatim, commissioned 1976. UTG's chronology entry (verified by direct fetch of the archived page) reads: '1976 р. Введено в експлуатацію магістральний газопровід Івацевичі - Долина (І нитка) довжиною 357,7 км, ∅1220 мм' -- diameter matches GEM (1220mm) and confirms this is a real, separately-commissioned pipe with its own year and length, distinct from string II. Owner attribution ('Gazprom PJSC') for the Belarusian half is defensible at the parent level: ru.wikipedia confirms Gazprom PJSC acquired 50% of Beltransgaz in 2007 and the remaining 50% in Nov 2011, becoming 100% owner of what is now Gazprom Transgaz Belarus -- but that operating subsidiary, not 'Gazprom PJSC' directly, is the actual titleholder; a minor precision note, not an error worth escalating.

rows.recommendation: Same disposition as P3484: not a duplicate, but shares the same two sourcing defects (system capacity restated as this string's own, and an unsupported/likely-wrong length citation). Additionally flag for Update: StartYear1=1981 does not match any commissioning date found in sourcing -- UTG's own chronology dates the 'ІІ нитка' (line II) to 1977, not 1981, immediately following the 1976 entry for line I. Before changing StartYear1, check whether 1981 corresponds to a real later event (a specific capacity upgrade, a documented later completion of some section) that this pass did not find, or is a data artifact; do not silently overwrite either year without a fresh source.
rows.notes: UTG chronology entry (same source as P3484, directly verified): '1977 р. ... Введено в експлуатацію магістральний газопровід Івацевичі - Долина (ІІ нитка) довжиною 366,7 км, ∅1220 мм.' Diameter matches GEM; length (366.7 km) is DIFFERENT from both GEM's stated 292.00 km AND from string I's own 357.7 km -- i.e. per the primary operator source the two strings are not even identical to each other in length, contrary to what GEM's identical 292.00/292.00 currently implies. Independent confirmation that line II is a genuinely separate, distinct physical structure (not a duplicate record of line I): a peer-reviewed 2011 engineering-inspection paper (Banakhevych, Krupka, Marchuk, 'Theory and Practice of Construction' no.7, KNUBA) is specifically about a diagnostic survey of 'МГ Івацевичі-Долина ІІ н.' (line II)'s own cable-stayed Dniester river crossing -- a structure that exists and needed its own inspection precisely because it is a physically distinct pipe, not a bookkeeping duplicate. OpenStreetMap's mapped way for this corridor is tagged 'double wires', consistent with a two-parallel-pipe corridor drawn as one trace (matching the pre-fetched geometry finding that both rows share one 15-vertex, 480.29 km schematic trace -- a shared-corridor convention, not evidence of duplication).

rows.recommendation: No action needed. Checked per the cluster brief's hub question and found P0779 ('Torzhok-Smolensk-Mazyr-Dolyna', 1300.00 km, 1420mm, 22.00 bcm/y) does NOT overlap or double-count against P3484/P5938 ('Ivatsevichy-Kobryn-Dolyna' I/II, 1220mm). They are two genuinely distinct, separately-named corridors into Dolyna.
rows.notes: The same independent ISANS 2023 report that covers the Ivatsevichi-Dolyna corridor separately and explicitly names TWO different Torzhok-origin lines reaching Dolyna: '...магистральный газопровод «Торжок — Долина» диаметром 1420 мм (около 22 млрд куб.м. в год)' (routed via Smolensk/Mazyr per P0779's own name) versus '...двухниточным магистральным газопроводом «Ивацевичи — Долина» диаметром 1220 мм (около 30 млрд куб. м. в год)' (the P3484/P5938 corridor, via Minsk/Ivatsevichi/Kobryn). P0779's own sheet values (1420mm, 22.00 bcm/y) match the ISANS 'Torzhok-Dolyna' figures exactly, corroborating both that this ref is correctly cited for P0779 and that it is a real, separate physical pipeline on a different route with a different diameter than the Ivatsevichy-Kobryn-Dolyna pair. No further action; this closes the hub question raised in the brief.

'Bilche-Wolitz-Dolyna', 68.00 km, 1400mm -- different origin (Bilche-Volytsia gas storage facility, within Ukraine), different diameter, roughly 1/4 the length. No plausible overlap with the Ivatsevichy-Kobryn-Dolyna cluster or with P0779; a distinct short domestic connector into the Dolyna hub. Not investigated further beyond this scope check, per the brief's instruction not to over-invest in the hub.

'Bohorodchany-Dolyna', 42.00 km, 1400mm -- different origin (Bohorodchany, within Ukraine), different diameter, short domestic connector. No plausible overlap with the Ivatsevichy-Kobryn-Dolyna cluster or P0779. Not investigated further beyond this scope check.

sources.what: Central Dispatch Administration of the Russian Fuel and Energy Complex (cdu.ru), 'Газовая промышленность Белоруссии' -- explicitly characterizes the corridor as 'Ивацевичи — Долина (2х1220 мм)', a two-line 1220mm system, and separately 'Торжок — Минск — Ивацевичи (3х1220 мм)' as the preceding three-line Belarusian trunk. Independent Russian federal energy-sector source corroborating the two-string structure.

ISANS (Belarusian independent analytical center), 'Энергоснабжение Беларуси' report, 2023 -- this is GEM's OWN cited ref for LengthKnownKm/Diameter on P3484/P5938, so it was independently re-verified rather than taken on trust: downloaded directly and full-text-extracted with pdftotext. Confirms (p.25): 'Украина и Беларусь связаны двухниточным магистральным газопроводом «Ивацевичи — Долина» диаметром 1220 мм (около 30 млрд куб. м. в год)' -- i.e. explicitly states the ~30 bcm/y figure as the TOTAL for the whole two-line system, and gives diameter 1220mm, but contains NO length-in-km figure anywhere for this pipeline -- the ref does not support the 292.00 km value it is cited for on either row. Also confirms (p.19) the separate 'Торжок — Долина' line at 1420mm / ~22 bcm/y, matching P0779 exactly. NOTE: url_verifier.py FAILs the Cyrillic-substring check on this PDF (a documented false-negative pattern for PDFs whose extracted text the verifier's own fetcher does not parse identically to a direct pdftotext extraction) -- content was independently confirmed by local extraction, not by the verifier's automated check.

open_questions: Is there a genuine, separately-existing THIRD string ('ІІІ нитка') on this corridor that GEM does not track at all? UTG's own chronology has a 1979 entry explicitly labeled 'Івацевичі - Долина (ІІІ нитка)' at 17.8 km/1220mm -- but that length is far too short to be a full parallel string comparable to line I (357.7 km) or line II (366.7 km), and a preceding unlabeled 1977 entry gives another short 23.8 km/1220mm figure for the same corridor. These may be short tie-in/completion segments that finished commissioning of an already-mostly-built line within Ukrainian territory in stages, rather than evidence of a whole missing third trunk -- this pass could not resolve which. If a genuine third string does exist and is missing from GEM, that is a Discovery question, not a redundancy question, per the cluster brief -- flagged here for the record, not chased further in this pass.

What does UTG's chronology length actually measure -- the FULL corridor border-to-border (Belarus + Ukraine), or only the commissioning length within what was then the Ukrainian SSR? Neither 357.7 km nor 366.7 km matches the drawn 480.29 km end-to-end trace nor GEM's stated 292.00 km, and no source in this pass settled which territorial extent UTG's own figures represent. This needs a source specifically on the Belarusian-territory portion (e.g. Gazprom Transgaz Belarus's own asset list) to settle -- belarus-tr.gazprom.ru refused every connection attempt in this pass (network-level ECONNREFUSED, not a confirmed take-down; worth retrying from a different network/session before concluding it is unreachable).
What does P5938's StartYear1=1981 actually correspond to, given UTG's own chronology dates line II's commissioning to 1977? Not resolved in this pass.
summary: GEM's P3484 (SegmentName 'I', StartYear1 1976) and P5938 (SegmentName 'II', StartYear1 1981) record the 'Ivatsevichy-Kobryn-Dolyna Gas Pipeline' as two rows that are byte-identical on length (292.00 km), diameter (1220mm) and capacity (29.00 bcm/y) -- the tracker's canonical parallel-strings structural signature. Per this cluster's governing discipline, that signature alone proves nothing either way, and here the sourcing comes down decisively on the REFUTED side: Ukrtransgaz's own official construction chronology (the operator's corporate history, archived and independently full-text-extracted in this pass) names and dates the two strings SEPARATELY -- 'Івацевичі-Долина (І нитка)', commissioned 1976, 357.7 km; 'Івацевичі-Долина (ІІ нитка)', commissioned 1977, 366.7 km -- both at 1220mm. A 2011 peer-reviewed engineering paper independently confirms line II has its own dedicated cable-stayed river crossing over the Dniester requiring its own diagnostic inspection, which only makes sense if it is a physically distinct structure. Russia's federal fuel-and-energy dispatch body (cdu.ru) independently characterizes the whole corridor as 'Ивацевичи — Долина (2х1220 мм)' -- a two-line system. This is the documented Soviet parallel-strings pattern (as in the comparable, already-adjudicated Kazakh cluster), not a duplicate. Verdict: DUPLICATE_REFUTED. However, chasing this hypothesis surfaced two real, separate data-quality defects that the duplicate question does not resolve on its own, matching exactly the two things the cluster brief asked to check. First: CAPACITY IS DOUBLE-COUNTED. GEM's own prior researcher note on P3484 already says '[t]he capacity number is total for the pipeline' -- and an independent 2023 Belarusian analytical report (ISANS), which happens to be GEM's own pre-existing citation for this row (independently re-verified here rather than trusted on faith), states in its own words that the whole two-line corridor carries about 30 bcm/y total. So the 29.00 bcm/y appearing on BOTH rows is one system figure restated twice -- summing the two rows overstates corridor capacity by roughly double (58 vs. ~29-30). Second: THE LENGTH FIGURE IS UNSOURCED AND LIKELY WRONG. The same ISANS PDF that GEM cites as the ref for LengthKnownKm=292.00 on both rows was independently downloaded and full-text-extracted for this pass, and it contains NO length-in-km figure for this pipeline anywhere -- only diameter and the system-total capacity. Meanwhile UTG's own chronology gives each string a DIFFERENT length (357.7 vs. 366.7 km), neither matching 292.00 km and, notably, not matching each other either -- directly contradicting GEM's current identical-292.00-km-on-both-rows treatment. Neither defect changes the duplicate verdict, but both are real, actionable Update-leg findings: fix or flag the capacity double-count, and re-source the length field using the UTG chronology rather than the miscited ISANS ref. A tertiary Owner-attribution note: 'Gazprom PJSC' is defensible as the ultimate parent (confirmed 100% owner of the Belarusian operating subsidiary since Nov 2011) but the direct titleholder, Gazprom Transgaz Belarus, is not named -- minor, not escalation-worthy. The Dolyna-hub secondary check clears cleanly: P0779 ('Torzhok-Smolensk-Mazyr-Dolyna', 1420mm/22 bcm/y) is confirmed by the same ISANS source as a genuinely separate, differently-routed, differently-dimensioned corridor (matching the source's own explicit distinction between the 1420mm 'Torzhok-Dolyna' line and the 1220mm 'Ivatsevichi-Dolyna' pair), and P1462/P1463 are unrelated short domestic connectors at a different diameter. One open thread intentionally left unchased per the brief's Discovery/redundancy boundary: UTG's chronology also records two short, oddly-sized 1977/1979 entries (23.8 km and 'ІІІ нитка' 17.8 km) on this same corridor that do not fit cleanly as either full third strings or as explained remainders of I/II -- flagged for a possible Discovery follow-up, not resolved here.
